To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the plasma membrane of human neutrophils is highly Ca2(+)-sensitive and (2) Ca2(+)-stimulated fusion of the plasma membranes is enhanced by GTP gamma S.

(a) Ca2+ promotes fusion between neutrophil plasma and liposomes, (b) Ca2+ is a more effective stimulus for this fusion than other divalent cation species, and (c) the neutrophil fusion process is distinct from that of red blood cells.

the inside-out plasma membrane-enrichment fraction from neutrophils is capable of fusing (in the absence of any exogenous protein) with artificial lipid membranes, and this fusion is dependent upon micromolar concentrations (2-50 microM) of Ca2+, and is not observed with other divalent cation species (Mg2+, Ba2+, and Sr2+) even at high (millimolar) concentrations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Ca(2+)-dependent membrane fusion in neutrophil function.
identifying the factors which regulate the fusion of neutrophil plasma with granule membranes.
the mechanism by which Ca2+ stimulates neutrophil plasma-membrane fusion with liposomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

neutrophil membranes are capable of Ca2(+)-induced membrane fusion, and that the fusion is highly specific for Ca(2+) and is dependent upon a specific membrane protein (or proteins) which is not present in RBC membranes.

Ca2+ is required for fusion of neutrophil plasma-membrane-enriched fractions with liposomes and that this Ca2(+)-stimulated fusion is not due to a nonspecific Ca2(+)-induced perturbation of membrane structure.
Ca2+ is a potent stimulator of neutrophil plasma-membrane-liposome fusion, and this process may play a role in the exocytosis of the neutrophils' granules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ca2(+)-induced fusion of neutrophil plasma-membrane enriched fractions with liposomes is a Ca2(+)- and GTP gamma S-dependent process which may be mediated by a Ca2(+), GTP gamma S-regulated protein.
Ca2(+)-induced fusion of neutrophil membranes is not dependent upon the integrity of spectrin, and is not a general phenomenon occurring with all cells.

neutrophil plasma (outside-out) membranes are capable of Ca(2+)-dependent fusion with liposomes, whereas RBC membranes (inside-out or outside-out) do not fuse with liposome in the absence of spectrin depletion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neutrophil membrane fraction can fuse with liposomes and that this process is Ca2+ dependent.
neutrophil membranes can fuse with artificial lipid membranes.
the fusion of neutrophil plasma with artificial lipid membranes is highly dependent upon Ca2+.
